name: Norway (Oslo)
kernel_gaps: Social: continuous phase-in cap (contribution <= k x (income - floor)) instead of an all-or-nothing floor (trygdeavgift, ftrl. § 23-3 (4))
Taper with two steps and a falling rate (pension credit 16.7 % then 6 %, sktl. § 16-1 (3))
Ceiling on a group of taxes as a share of income above a limit, with a wealth add-on (skattebegrensning, sktl. § 17-1)
Dual: owner income grossed up (x1.72) inside the one flat base, not a separate capital schedule (sktl. §§ 10-11, 10-31)

validation.notes: 8 family types x 6 lines; max gap 6.3 NOK (THP), all from rounding each tax down to the krone vs OECD unrounded figures; 45/48 within 5 NOK

validation.referee: OECD TW 2025 via kernel oecd_check20.py (generic mapping)
validation.notes: independent run of the kernel harness; THP 8/8 within 1 %

validation.referee: Official worked examples and published figures (Skatteetaten satser 2025, trekkrutine test, OECD STA)
validation.notes: 37.84 % on gains/dividends/losses; max METRs 47.4/44.8/50.6/47.8 %; skjermingsrente 3.6/4.6 %; 144 003; STA 200 550

validation.referee: Skatteetaten trekkrutine 2025 (open code, Python port) vs Skatteetaten's published 2025 table file
validation.notes: port fidelity: every published row of tables 8000-8400 and 9010-9400 reproduced

validation.referee: Withholding tables (table 8000, monthly) vs statute model
validation.notes: tables never under-withhold; up to 2 434 NOK/yr over, all from the tables' 88 % minstefradrag (F1)

headline: Norway's 2025 income tax in Lean matches the OECD's Norwegian rows to within rounding and reproduces Skatteetaten's published withholding tables row for row; the tables over-withhold about 2 430 NOK a year by deducting only 88 % of the minstefradrag, sole traders earning 108 550-176 684 NOK face a 47 % marginal rate, and four cross-references in skatteloven are stale.
